s0302.literal: [Three] years, the prince was established as crown prince—supplemented and emended according to the Basic Annals of Emperor Wu in the History of Liang.
s0302.idiomatic: On "[three] years, the prince was established as crown prince": emended per the Basic Annals of Emperor Wu in the History of Liang.

s0305.literal: [Crow] streams calamity—changed according to Xu Xiaomu's Collected Works and Yan Kejun's Collected Chen Documents.
s0305.idiomatic: On "[crow] streams calamity": emended per Xu Xiaomu's Collected Works and Yan Kejun's Collected Chen Documents.

s0306.literal: Comment: tradition says there is a crow in the sun, as in the Spiritual Teachings chapter of the Huainanzi.
s0306.idiomatic: Tradition says there is a crow in the sun, as in Huainanzi, Spiritual Teachings.

s0307.literal: Also tradition says that in Yao's time ten suns appeared together and plants withered; Yao ordered Yi to shoot upward at the ten suns, hit nine, and the crows all died and fell with their wings—as cited in Northern Hall Manuscripts 149, Literary Gatherings 1, and Imperial Readings 3 quoting the Huainanzi.
s0307.idiomatic: Tradition also says ten suns rose in Yao's time, plants withered, and Yao had Yi shoot nine of them so the crows fell—cited in Northern Hall Manuscripts 149, Literary Gatherings 1, and Imperial Readings 3 from Huainanzi.

s0308.literal: This is the source of the phrase.
s0308.idiomatic: That is the source of the phrase.

s0309.literal: [4] Now Yuechang stands remote—"Yuechang" in all editions reads "Yueshang."
s0309.idiomatic: On "now Yuechang stands remote": all editions read Yueshang for Yuechang.

s0310.literal: Comment: chang and shang are ancient and modern forms of the same word.
s0310.idiomatic: Chang and shang are ancient and modern forms of the same word.

s0311.literal: [5] Springs flow, treasure bowls—"bowl" in Wu Zhaoyi's annotated Xu Xiaomu Collection reads "vessel," with a note citing Forest of Literary Arts citing Woodcutter on Mountains, saying the Treasure Vessel Spring issues from Jiangzhou.
s0311.idiomatic: On "springs flow, treasure bowls": Wu Zhaoyi's annotated Xu Xiaomu Collection reads vessel for bowl, citing Forest of Literary Arts and Woodcutter on Mountains on the Treasure Vessel Spring at Jiangzhou.

s0312.literal: [6] Again, these guest-travelers—below "this" both Yuan Gui 663 and the annotated Xu Xiaomu Collection have the character "segment."
s0312.idiomatic: On "again, these guest-travelers": Yuan Gui 663 and the annotated Xu Xiaomu Collection add segment below this.

s0313.literal: [7] Four tombs dismembering Chiyou—"four" should read "three."
s0313.idiomatic: On "four tombs dismembering Chiyou": four should read three.

s0314.literal: Tradition says Yao dismembered Chiyou, body and head in different places, buried in three sites—the head tomb at Shouyang, the shoulder tomb at Shanyang, the thigh tomb at Julu—as in Cloud Book Seven Talismans citing Records of the Yellow Emperor; this is the source of the phrase.
s0314.idiomatic: Tradition says Yao dismembered Chiyou and buried head, shoulders, and thighs at Shouyang, Shanyang, and Julu—Cloud Book Seven Talismans citing Records of the Yellow Emperor is the source.

s0315.literal: The Basic Annals of Emperor Yuan in the History of Liang records Xu Ling's petition urging accession, which also has "Chiyou's three tombs—can one call it stern execution?"
s0315.idiomatic: Liang Emperor Yuan's annals record Xu Ling's accession petition with the same "Chiyou's three tombs—can one call it stern execution?"

s0316.literal: [8] Again heard that this dynasty's princesses—"princesses" in Xu Xiaomu's Collected Works and Yan's Collected Chen Documents both read "princes and dukes"; probably "princes and dukes" is correct.
s0316.idiomatic: On "again heard that this dynasty's princesses": Xu Xiaomu's Collection and Yan's Collected Chen Documents read princes and dukes; that is probably correct.

s0317.literal: [9] Chunchun jingjing—Yan's Collected Chen Documents reads "native hamlet, native district."
s0317.idiomatic: On "chunchun jingjing": Yan's Collected Chen Documents reads native hamlet, native district.

s0318.literal: [10] Yu Ge showed the way—"ge" in all editions reads "song."
s0318.idiomatic: On "Yu Ge showed the way": all editions read song for ge.

s0319.literal: Comment: ge is the ancient form of the character for song.
s0319.idiomatic: Ge is the ancient form of the character for song.

s0320.literal: [11] I know its secret—"secret" should read "formula."
s0320.idiomatic: On "I know its secret": secret (jue) should read formula (jue).

s0321.literal: The current Xu Xiaomu Collection and Yan's Collected Chen Documents both read "formula."
s0321.idiomatic: Current Xu Xiaomu Collection and Yan's Collected Chen Documents both read formula.

s0322.literal: [12] Besides, greasy lips and vending tongues—"vending tongue" in Wu Zhaoyi's annotated Xu Xiaomu Collection is changed to "wiping tongue," the note citing the Biography of the eunuch Lü Qiang in Later Han: "the wicked crane their necks, greasy lips wipe tongue."
s0322.idiomatic: On "greasy lips and vending tongues": Wu Zhaoyi's annotated Xu Xiaomu Collection reads wiping tongue, citing Later Han, Biography of Lü Qiang: "the wicked crane their necks, greasy lips wipe tongue."

s0323.literal: [13] None fail to honor lord and kin to inscribe things—"inscribe" in the current Xu Xiaomu Collection and Yan's Collected Chen Documents reads "charge."
s0323.idiomatic: On "none fail to honor lord and kin to inscribe things": current Xu Xiaomu Collection and Yan's Collected Chen Documents read charge for inscribe.

s0324.literal: [14] Touring provinces to transform customs—the current Xu Xiaomu Collection and Yan's Collected Chen Documents read "touring the regions to inspect transformation"; as touring the regions pairs with the eastern and western sequences below, "touring the regions" is correct.
s0324.idiomatic: On "touring provinces to transform customs": current texts read touring the regions to inspect transformation, which pairs with eastern and western sequences below and is correct.

s0325.literal: [15] Eastern sequence, western college—the annotated Xu Xiaomu Collection changes to "western sequence, eastern college," citing Royal Regulations: "The Xia housed common elders in the western sequence; Zhou housed state elders in the eastern college."
s0325.idiomatic: On "eastern sequence, western college": the annotated Xu Xiaomu Collection reads western sequence, eastern college, citing Royal Regulations on Xia and Zhou elder care.

s0326.literal: [16] Not leopard, not bear—"leopard" in Wu Zhaoyi's annotated Xu Xiaomu Collection and Yan's Collected Chen Documents reads "tiger."
s0326.idiomatic: On "not leopard, not bear": annotated Xu Xiaomu Collection and Yan's Collected Chen Documents read tiger for leopard.

s0327.literal: Comment: the phrase comes from Announcement of Mu: "Be bold and martial, like tigers, like bears."
s0327.idiomatic: The phrase comes from Announcement of Mu: "Be bold and martial, like tigers, like bears."

s0328.literal: The History of Liang, Emperor Yuan's annals, records Ling's petition urging accession also has "not tiger, not bear."
s0328.idiomatic: Liang Emperor Yuan's annals record Xu Ling's accession petition with the same "not tiger, not bear."

s0329.literal: This reads "leopard" because of alteration to avoid Tang taboo.
s0329.idiomatic: Leopard here is a Tang-taboo alteration.

s0330.literal: [17] At that time Prince of Ancheng Xu was minister of works—"Xu" was originally written "taboo name"; Sizhi's original text is so; now changed according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.
s0330.idiomatic: On "at that time Prince of Ancheng Xu was minister of works": Xu was written taboo name in Yao Sizhi's original; emended per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.

s0331.literal: [18] Duty officer Bao Shenrui abused the prince's authority—"Bao Shenrui" in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions reads "Bao Shurui."
s0331.idiomatic: On "duty officer Bao Shenrui abused the prince's authority": Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions read Bao Shurui.

s0332.literal: [19] In the third year he was promoted to left vice minister of the Secretariat—"third year" in all editions is erroneously "second year."
s0332.idiomatic: On "in the third year he was promoted to left vice minister of the Secretariat": all editions wrongly read second year.

s0333.literal: Comment: in Emperor Xuan's annals, third year, first month, guichou, Xu Ling as right vice minister of the Secretariat and director of the great works was made vice minister of the Secretariat; fourth year, first month, bingwu, as vice minister of the Secretariat and director of the great works he was made left vice minister—this differs.
s0333.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan's annals place Xu Ling's promotion to vice minister in year 3, guichou, and to left vice minister in year 4, bingwu—not as here.

s0334.literal: [20] Jian's other name was Zhong—the Hall edition's textual verification says: "'Zhong' in the Southern History reads 'Bao.'"
s0334.idiomatic: On "Jian's other name was Zhong": the Hall edition notes the Southern History reads Bao for Zhong.
